dedupe_keys.name: nyc fire incident dispatch data fdny starfire computer aided dispatch

description: This dataset contains one record per fire incident created in the Fire Department of New York City's Starfire computer aided dispatch system, from creation of the incident to its close. It is published by the FDNY on the NYC Open Data portal. Each record gives the Starfire incident identifier, date and time, alarm box borough, number and location, alarm source, alarm level and highest alarm level, incident classification and group (structural fire, non-structural fire, medical emergency, non-medical emergency), times of first assignment, activation and arrival on scene, dispatch, travel and total response seconds with validity flags, and the number of engines, ladders and other units assigned. Coverage is the five boroughs from 2005 onwards and the table is refreshed a few times a year. The data are free through the Socrata SODA API or as CSV and JSON exports under the NYC Open Data terms of use. Caveats: exact incident addresses are withheld and incidents are located only by alarm box, zip code and administrative districts, and response-time fields should be filtered on their validity flags. Simulation uses: calibrating fire station coverage and unit deployment models, measuring demand by alarm level and time, and planning for surge and station closures. Related records: the companion FDNY EMS Incident Dispatch Data (data-nyc-fdny-ems-incident-dispatch) and the London Fire Brigade incident records (data-london-fire-brigade-incident-records) as a comparable city feed.
